title: Drive Radio — August 10, 2026
description:
- Taxi drivers rarely die of Alzheimer's: A wild dive into how spatial navigation physically grows the hippocampus — and what GPS-dependence might be doing to our brains. (https://theconversation.com/taxi-drivers-rarely-die-of-alzheimers-how-complex-mental-maps-and-spatial-reasoning-protect-your-brain-286650)
- Over 181,000 AI meeting recordings left wide open: An exposed backend at a popular AI note-taker shows how fast 'convenient' AI tools can turn into a massive privacy leak. (https://bobdahacker.com/blog/tldv-hack)
- 50k Boat Names: A delightfully pointless dataset of tens of thousands of real boat names, because not every story needs a moral. (https://www.beautifulpublicdata.com/boat-names/)
- Docker Sandboxes: Docker's new disposable environments for AI agents signal a big shift: infrastructure built to contain code written by AI, not humans. (https://www.docker.com/products/docker-sandboxes/)
- Because It's Not Fun Enough: why languages fail: A sharp argument that programming languages succeed or die based on how fun they are to use, not how technically sound they are. (https://bytecode.news/posts/2026/08/because-it-s-not-fun-enough)

title: Drive Radio — August 9, 2026
description:
- My server is a phone now: A dead Android phone gets a second life as a full-blown home server, battery and all — the ultimate e-waste hack. (https://seg6.space/posts/phone-server/)
- _for-sale DNS records: A quietly clever new DNS record lets domain owners advertise 'this is for sale' directly in the internet's plumbing. (https://specification.website/spec/foundations/for-sale-dns/)
- CSS: The bomb inside your inbox: Turns out the 'harmless' styling language can crash mail clients and leak data — no JavaScript required. (https://portswigger.net/research/css-the-bomb-inside-your-inbox)
- Amazon circumvents Gilroy community vote for AI data center: A 45-year-old procedural rule lets Amazon sidestep public comment on a massive new AI data center. (https://www.tomshardware.com/tech-industry/data-centers/amazon-secretly-circumvents-community-vote-for-massive-ai-data-center-45-year-old-rules-lock-gilroy-residents-out-of-public-comment-window)
- Everything You Do Is Being Recorded: AI wearables are creating a new always-listening reality — and a whole new etiquette war around it. (https://www.theatlantic.com/technology/2026/05/ai-wearable-surveillance-countermeasures/687203/)

title: Drive Radio — August 8, 2026
description:
- Now we have a timeline of the OpenAI accidental attack against Hugging Face: A forensic timeline reveals how an autonomous OpenAI system accidentally DDoS'd Hugging Face — a scary preview of machine-speed mistakes with no human in the loop. (https://simonwillison.net/2026/Aug/7/openai-timeline/)
- New Amazon Data Center Is Set to Have the Most Polluting Power Plant in the U.S.: The AI boom's carbon cost just got a literal address, as Amazon pairs a new Texas data center with what could be the country's dirtiest power plant. (https://www.nytimes.com/2026/08/08/climate/amazon-data-center-texas-pollution.html)
- The Nixpkgs core team has disbanded: The volunteer team steering NixOS's massive package ecosystem just walked away, exposing how fragile open-source infrastructure really is. (https://discourse.nixos.org/t/the-nixpkgs-core-team-has-disbanded/79413)
- Hardware backdoors in some x86 CPUs: Researchers exposed a hidden, undocumented processor core in certain x86 chips that can bypass all normal security — a literal backdoor in silicon. (https://github.com/xoreaxeaxeax/rosenbridge)
- DeepMind's WeatherNext model achieves breakthrough forecasting cyclones: AI is now beating traditional physics models at predicting cyclone paths, giving coastal communities crucial extra days of warning. (https://deepmind.google/blog/weathernext-ai-model-achieves-breakthrough-in-forecasting-cyclones/)
- NASA figured out how to keep its Voyager 2 probe running for another year: Forty-eight years and twelve billion miles from home, Voyager 2 gets one more clever power trick to keep phoning Earth. (https://www.space.com/space-exploration/voyager/nasa-figured-out-how-to-keep-its-48-year-old-voyager-2-probe-running-for-yet-another-year)

title: Drive Radio — August 7, 2026
description:
- US strikes $1.2B deal to pay German firm to halt offshore wind projects: The government paid nine figures just to make sure a wind farm never gets built — a wild snapshot of current energy politics. (https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c1e1vg0gjl5o)
- Mario Meets Pareto: A viral deep-dive applies the 80/20 rule to Super Mario level design and accidentally explains why some games just feel better. (https://www.mayerowitz.io/blog/mario-meets-pareto)
- AMD acquires Taalas to boost inference performance by etching models in silicon: AMD's buying a startup that literally burns AI models into chips — a bold bet on speed over flexibility. (https://www.theregister.com/systems/2026/08/06/amd-acquires-ai-chip-startup-taalas-to-boost-inference-performance-by-etching-models-into-silicon/5284344)
- New Mexico court orders Meta to pay $567m over harms to children's mental health: A landmark ruling that's small money for Meta but potentially huge legal precedent. (https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/aug/06/new-mexico-court-meta)
- Radical Study Suggests Life on Earth Arose Twice: New research suggests life may have sparked from non-living matter more than once — reshaping how we think about life elsewhere in the universe. (https://www.sciencealert.com/radical-study-suggests-life-on-earth-arose-from-non-living-matter-twice)
- U.S. economy lost 23,000 jobs in July, a sudden reversal: A confusing jobs report where the headline number and the real story point in opposite directions. (https://www.nbcnews.com/business/economy/july-2026-jobs-report-rcna591138)

description:
